# Screening a list of companies

> A list of names came in from procurement. Which entries need a closer look?

This is the question the server was built for. Paste the list, get one row per company, and spend your attention on the rows with something on them.

The behaviour worth studying is what happens to the awkward entries. A name matching several companies is never guessed at: it comes back under `unresolved` with its candidates so you can ask which was meant. Nothing is dropped to make the table tidy.

> **About the responses below.** They are real output from this server — every
> call on this page is executed when the documentation is generated, and
> whatever comes back is what you see. The upstream data comes from fixtures
> recorded from the live Companies House API, so the companies are real and
> the facts are public record. Open Government Licence v3.0 applies to eligible information,
> excluding personal data and other OGL exceptions. The framing around them is illustrative: this project makes no claim
> about any company or person named here beyond what the register itself
> states.

## Walkthrough

### 1. screen_companies

Pass the list exactly as it arrived — company numbers, full names and half-remembered names mixed together.

```json
{
  "tool": "screen_companies",
  "arguments": {
    "companies": [
      "04138203",
      "Royal Mail Limited",
      "Royal Mail"
    ]
  }
}
```

```json

  "requested": 3,
  "sections_used": [
    "profile",
    "charges",
    "insolvency"
  ],
  "screened": [
    {
      "input": "04138203",
      "company_number": "04138203",
      "name": "ROYAL MAIL GROUP LIMITED",
      "status": "active",
      "incorporated_on": "2001-01-10",
      "age_years": 25,
      "signal_codes": [
        "outstanding_charges"
      ],
      "signal_count": 1,
      "sections_included": [
        "profile",
        "charges",
        "insolvency"
      ],
      "sections_unavailable": [],
      "meta": {
        "cached": false,
        "stale": false,
        "rate_limit_remaining": 562,
        "rate_limit_resets_in_ms": 0,
        "licence": "OGL-v3.0"
      }
    },
    {
      "input": "Royal Mail Limited",
      "company_number": "14240638",
      "name": "ROYAL MAIL LIMITED",
      "status": "active",
      "incorporated_on": "2022-07-18",
      "age_years": 4,
      "signal_codes": [],
      "signal_count": 0,
      "sections_included": [
        "profile",
        "charges",
        "insolvency"
      ],
      "sections_unavailable": [],
      "meta": {
        "cached": false,
        "stale": false,
        "rate_limit_remaining": 562,
        "rate_limit_resets_in_ms": 0,
        "licence": "OGL-v3.0"
      }
    }
  ],
  "unresolved": [
    {
      "input": "Royal Mail",
      "reason": "5 companies match this name and none matches it exactly. Ask which was meant rather than assuming.",
      "candidates": [
        {
          "company_number": "14240638",
          "name": "ROYAL MAIL LIMITED",
          "status": "active"
        },
        {
          "company_number": "08680755",
          "name": "INTERNATIONAL DISTRIBUTION SERVICES LIMITED",
          "status": "active"
        },
        {
          "company_number": "03087786",
          "name": "RM (INTERNATIONAL) LIMITED",
          "status": "active"
        },
        {
          "company_number": "06307726",
          "name": "ROYAL MAIL COURIER SERVICES LTD",
          "status": "active"
        },
        {
          "company_number": "03693913",
          "name": "ROYAL MAIL ENTERPRISES LIMITED",
          "status": "active"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "not_screened": [],
  "meta": {
    "cached": false,
    "stale": false,
    "rate_limit_remaining": 562,
    "rate_limit_resets_in_ms": 0,
    "licence": "OGL-v3.0"
  }
}
```

Read it in three parts.

`screened` holds the rows that resolved cleanly, each with its signal codes. A `signal_count` of zero means nothing on the signal list was found — not that the company is sound.

`unresolved` is the row to act on. "Royal Mail" matches thousands of companies and none exactly, so the server stopped and handed back candidates rather than picking one. That refusal is the point: a plausible wrong company number returns a real company that nothing downstream would flag.

`sections_used` says what the signals could see. Officers are off by default because they cost an extra request per company; pass `include_officers: true` when the question is about who runs these businesses rather than what is registered against them.

## Notes

**If the list is long.** The limit is 600 requests per five minutes and screening costs three per company by default. `screen_companies` works out what it can afford, screens that, and returns the rest under `not_screened` with the reset time — so a table that comes back short always says why.
